summary: Remote WebSocket-controlled PTY shell and filesystem/git control on the installer's host
details: The package runs a long-lived agent that connects to a configured WebSocket server using a shared secret and routes server-sent messages into a spawned PTY (bash on Unix, PowerShell on Windows). The message router in message-router.js dispatches 'terminal_input' frames to terminal.js, which writes the WebSocket bytes directly to pty.write, giving the remote party an interactive shell on the host. The same router exposes handlers for arbitrary file read/write/create/delete/move/copy, git add/reset/restore/commit/push, upload_to_dir, and transfer_files, allowing full filesystem manipulation of the installer's machine. An 'upgrade_agent' message causes the agent to run `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` from a detached shell script and restart via systemd/launchd/PM2, letting the server swap the running agent code to whatever is currently published under the mutable `latest` tag. service/linux.js modifies PATH to include `~/.local/bin` and `~/.npm-global/bin` for persistence of the agent's own binaries. Anyone controlling the configured server, or holding the AGENT_SECRET, obtains full-host RCE on any machine running this agent.
